title: InstanceConfig
description: One file that defines an instance: branding, engine, surfaces, capability rules, auth, payments and content policy. Secrets never go here; they are environment variables.

name.description: Instance name shown in the interface.

logo.description: The instance's marks, as paths or URLs to images (SVG is best). Omitted, the name is set in type, and its first letter stands in for the symbol.

symbol.description: A square mark, for small places: the collapsed sidebar, sign-in and the agent's avatar.

wordmark.description: The full logo, for the open sidebar and headers.

tint.description: Draw the marks in the text colour, black in the light theme and white in the dark, using only their shape. Turn off for a logo in more than one colour, which then shows as drawn in both themes.

theme.description: Overrides for semantic colour tokens, per theme. Keys are token names without the leading dashes, e.g. "primary".

url.description: Engine REST API base URL. ENGINE_URL overrides it.

surfaces.description: Which parts of the product this instance serves.

mobile.description: The native iOS and Android apps. Off, the instance issues no device sessions and refuses requests that carry one.

mobileConsole.description: The operator console inside the native apps. Off, the instance issues no operator device sessions and refuses requests that carry one. Independent of mobile: a console-only instance turns this on alone.

mobile.description: The native apps built for this instance. Sign-in hands a finished session only to the apps named here.

bundleId.description: The iOS app's bundle identifier. Sign-in returns to <bundleId>://auth.

minimumVersion.description: Older builds are asked to update.

applicationId.description: The Android app's application id. Sign-in returns to <applicationId>://auth.

minimumVersion.description: Older builds are asked to update.

firebase.description: The Firebase project that sends this app its operator alerts, as the project's settings give it for the Android app. None of it is secret: the app is sent these and starts Firebase Cloud Messaging with them. The service account that sends is FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT in .env.

projectId.description: The project id, as in the service account's project_id.

appId.description: The Android app's id in the project, such as 1:1234567890:android:0a1b2c3d4e5f.

apiKey.description: The project's Android API key. It identifies the project; it authorises nothing by itself.

capabilities.description: Which discovered capabilities the instance offers. Patterns match app names; * matches any run of characters. Block wins over allow. An empty allow list allows everything.

overrides.description: Per-app overrides, keyed by app name.

methodParam.description: Authorization request parameter that tells the provider which method the user picked (for example "connection" or "kc_idp_hint").

methods.description: Sign-in methods offered on the sign-in screen, in order. The identity provider must support each one.

pricing.description: How wholesale network cost becomes credits charged.

adultContent.description: Allow adult content. Users still confirm their age and opt in.

retainChats.description: Keep prompts and outputs on the instance's servers.

backgroundVideo.description: URL or public path of a looping, silent video shown behind the home screen's composer.

backgroundPoster.description: Still image shown while the video loads, and in place of it when the visitor prefers reduced motion. With aurora, the opening frame shown while the live sky starts: the sky and stars without the aurora.

backgroundImage.description: URL or public path of a photograph shown behind the composer when there is no video, brought gently to life with a slow drift and a shimmer in its coloured light. With neither, soft drifting light is shown.

aurora.description: Draw a live aurora over backgroundImage, in place of any coloured glow in the photograph. Meant for a night-sky photo.
